review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of numEdges, graphConnected and genus in ChipFiringWithLean/Basic.lean. I grepped the uses of the num_edges_bridgeGraph_* lemmas across LeanPool, and I compared with the sibling vertexWedge simp interface. I found no looping or competing-rule problem. The @[simp] bridgeGraph_edges is rfl on an abbrev, which is harmless, and none of the simp lemmas overlap. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether the proposed lemma would fire without further changes in the downstream proofs. I judged the lack of simp attributes on bridgeGraph_edge_card and bridgeGraph_vertex_card too weak to report: neither lemma is used outside this file, and Fintype.card_sum is already a simp lemma. The one finding is the missing reverse-orientation cross-edge lemma.

findings.excerpt: if a = x ∧ b = y then 1 else 0
findings.problem: The simp interface covers numEdges for (inl,inl), (inr,inr) and (inl,inr), but not for (inr,inl). numEdges is symmetric in its arguments, but num_edges_symmetric is not a simp lemma (it would loop), so simp cannot normalise numEdges (bridgeGraph ..) (Sum.inr b) (Sum.inl a). Every downstream user has to rebuild the reversed fact by hand with `rw [num_edges_symmetric]; exact num_edges_bridgeGraph_inl_inr ...` or a local `hReverse...` helper. The sibling vertexWedge interface already provides the reversed lemma as a simp lemma, `num_edges_vertexWedge_right_left`. Note also that `num_edges_bridgeGraph_endpoints` is just the `a = x, b = y` instance of this lemma and is derived by `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Add right after `num_edges_bridgeGraph_inl_inr`: `@[simp] theorem num_edges_bridgeGraph_inr_inl (G H x y) (b : H.V) (a : G.V) : numEdges (bridgeGraph G H x y) (Sum.inr b) (Sum.inl a) = if a = x ∧ b = y then 1 else 0 := by rw [num_edges_symmetric]; exact num_edges_bridgeGraph_inl_inr G H x y a b`. Keep the condition in the same normal form `a = x ∧ b = y`, so that both orientations reduce to the same expression. Then drop the ad-hoc reversed copies at the use sites. These are TwoPole.lean `simp_rw [num_edges_symmetric, ...]` (which also rewrites other numEdges terms), BridgeDivisors.lean `hCross`, GraphConstructorIso.lean `rw [num_edges_symmetric, num_edges_bridgeGraph_inl_inr, num_edges_symmetric]`, BridgeCut.lean, and BridgeChainTransport.lean `hReverseFirst`/`hReverseTarget`.
findings.benefit: Users can simplify numEdges of the bridge graph in either orientation with plain `simp`. This removes the repeated symmetric-rewrite boilerplate, and the `simp_rw [num_edges_symmetric]` calls that rewrite every numEdges term and risk rewriting unrelated ones. It also brings the bridge interface in line with the vertexWedge one, and the in-file proof of `graph_connected_bridgeGraph` (line 180, `rw [num_edges_symmetric]; simp`) could close with `simp` alone.
